paragraphs: Yochanan, brother of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak the priest.
Hyman cites Semachot 4:11. When Yochanan’s brother Rabbi Shimon died, Yochanan came from Galilee intending to incur ritual impurity for him.

notes.text: The supplied text gives Semachot 4:1; the historical OCR provenance has a possible 4:11 reading. The priestly designation remains in its original syntactic position.

The saved whole Vilna 1883 Semachot chapter-4 scalar at index10 names Yochanan coming from Galilee after Shimon ben Yehotzadak died in Lod, supplying the corresponding 4:11 location alongside source 4:1. The intended impurity visit is bracketed in that text, which then reports a prohibition after closure; no permission is invented. The scalar lacks Hyman’s Rabbi/priest designations, whose source placement is retained. This is a textual comparison, not proof of the source’s halakhah glyph history.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 672) gives Semachot 4:11, where the supplied text gives 4:1. In the consulted passage Shimon ben Yehotzadak dies in Lod and his brother Yochanan comes from Galilee. The Hebrew brackets the words about his intention to incur impurity. The Sages ruled against doing so after the grave had been closed. Hyman places the priestly designation at the end of the heading.
